messages:
Lena Ortiz: Heads-up: Prospect (Kestrel Labs) wants a POC to migrate from PromptlyAI. Key asks: structured JSON parity, per-route billing, EU residency, and customer KMS. Can we enumerate blockers?
Chris Wang: Immediate blockers: seeded sampling parity, stop-token exactness, streaming truncation differences, and tokenization diffs for special chars. Also need to confirm Dedicated can do per-route metering and project tagging.
Aisha Rahman: Security checklist: KMS import support (HSM option), SOC2, DPA for EU data, redaction of PII in logs during POC. Legal wants a limited-scope DPA for proof-of-concept.
Lena Ortiz: Customer demands: 3-month committed Dedicated with migration credit if parity reached in 30 days. Also wants fallback webhooks if our model regresses.
Chris Wang: I'll own a harness: 50 prompts, 3 seeds each, stream vs non-stream, stop-token edgecases (nested markers). Acceptance goal: >=94% intent match and <4% higher hallucination than baseline.
Aisha Rahman: For POC infra: ephemeral credentials, no plaintext request retention, VPC peering only from their IPs. We'll share SOC2 and pen-test summary after DPA.
build-bot: cluster-provision: ephemeral-dedicated-eu-west created. Secrets staged to vault.
Chris Wang: Perf smoke plan: sustained 40 rps, burst to 150. I'll publish p50/p95 numbers and a curl example to reproduce.
Lena Ortiz: Owners: Chris (POC harness + perf), Aisha (security + DPA), Lena (customer comms + pricing). I'll draft email recapping timeline once legal confirms DPA timeline.
Aisha Rahman: One more: include token-diff examples for curly braces and emojis; these were pain points in their earlier migration.
Chris Wang: noted, will add a small token-diff report and example payloads.
Lena Ortiz: Thanks team. Closing for now, will reopen after legal updates.
